```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5
)
has_variants = requireNamespace("VariantAnnotation", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("SummarizedExperiment", quietly = TRUE)
```

## Introduction

`ggmethylation` visualises base modifications (5mC, 5hmC, 6mA, ...) on
individual long reads stored in modBAM format. It parses the MM/ML auxiliary
tags written by basecallers and tools such as dorado, pb-CpG-tools or modkit,
and `plot_methylation()` returns a `patchwork` figure with, from top to bottom:

- an optional **gene track** (`annotations`);
- the **read panel**: one horizontal bar per read, with a coloured mark at
  each modification site (colour encodes the modification probability);
- the **smooth panel**: the loess-smoothed mean modification probability per
  position, one line per group (or one overall line when the reads are not
  grouped), with a confidence ribbon;
- an optional **delta panel** (`show_delta = TRUE`) with the difference
  between two groups.

Reads can be grouped by any BAM auxiliary tag (e.g. the haplotype tag `HP`)
or by the base they carry at a user-supplied SNV. Grouping colours the read
bars and gives one smooth line per group, so the relationship between
haplotype or genotype and methylation is immediately visible.

**Index requirement.** `read_methylation()` queries reads by region with
`Rsamtools`, so the BAM needs an index (`.bai` or `.csi`, e.g. from
`samtools index`) next to it.

## Installation

```{r installation, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}
# Bioconductor dependencies
BiocManager::install(c("Rsamtools", "GenomicRanges", "IRanges"))

# Optional: VCF overlay and gene annotation track
BiocManager::install(c(
  "VariantAnnotation", "SummarizedExperiment",
  "GenomicFeatures", "txdbmaker", "rtracklayer", "AnnotationDbi"
))

# Install ggmethylation from GitHub
remotes::install_github("ljwharbers/ggmethylation")
```

## Example data

The package ships a small synthetic modBAM: about 70 reads on an 8 kb `chr1`
with 5mC (`m`) and 5hmC (`h`) calls, haplotype tags (`HP` 1 and 2, some reads
untagged), a 150 bp deletion carried by haplotype 1, a ~120 bp insertion at
`chr1:6100`, soft-clipped reads with supplementary alignments (SA tags), and
an A>G SNV at `chr1:3000` carried by haplotype 2. A matching VCF holds that
SNV, the deletion and a breakend. Every example below runs on these files;
replace the paths with your own BAM and VCF.

```{r data}
library(ggmethylation)

bam    = system.file("extdata", "synthetic.bam", package = "ggmethylation")
vcf    = system.file("extdata", "synthetic.vcf.gz", package = "ggmethylation")
region = "chr1:1000-7000"
```

## Basic usage

`read_methylation()` fetches the reads overlapping a region and returns a
`methylation_data` object. Secondary, duplicate and QC-fail alignments are
skipped; supplementary alignments are kept. When more than `max_reads`
(default 200) reads overlap the region a random subset is kept; pass `seed`
to make that choice reproducible.

```{r read-basic}
meth = read_methylation(bam, region, seed = 1)
meth
```

```{r plot-basic}
plot_methylation(meth)
```

Without grouping the smooth panel has one overall line. Soft-clipped reads
with a supplementary alignment get a small marker at the clipped end,
coloured by the chromosome of the SA partner, and reads with a large
deletion are drawn with a gap.

## The methylation_data object

`methylation_data` is a named list. `$reads` has one row per read, with its
displayed span (`start`/`end`, clipped to the region), its full alignment
span (`bam_pos`/`bam_end`), strand and supplementary-alignment information.
`$sites` has one row per read per modification call, with the reference
position and the modification probability (`ML / 255`).

```{r str-basic}
names(meth)
head(meth$reads)
head(meth$sites)
```

Calls on inserted bases have no reference coordinate and are kept separately
in `$insertion_sites` (see [Insertion loci](#insertion-loci)).

## Haplotype grouping (HP tag)

Phased reads (e.g. PacBio HiFi or ONT data haplotagged with WhatsHap) carry
a per-read haplotype tag. `group_tag = "HP"` groups reads by it; reads
without the tag form an `NA` group that is drawn in grey and not smoothed.

```{r read-hp}
meth_hp = read_methylation(bam, region, group_tag = "HP", seed = 1)
meth_hp
```

```{r plot-hp}
plot_methylation(meth_hp)
```

With exactly two groups, `show_delta = TRUE` adds a panel below the smooth
panel with the difference between the two smoothed curves (group 2 minus
group 1), filled with the colour of whichever group is higher. Where most
reads of a group carry the same large deletion, the smooth line and the
delta area are interrupted. Here `panel_heights` (read, smooth and delta
panel, top to bottom) gives the two summary panels a little more room than
the default.

```{r plot-delta, fig.height = 7}
plot_methylation(meth_hp, show_delta = TRUE, panel_heights = c(1, 0.4, 0.3))
```

Group colours are set with `group_colours`, a vector named by group. Groups
it does not name get further colour-blind-safe colours.

```{r plot-hp-colours}
plot_methylation(meth_hp, group_colours = c("1" = "steelblue", "2" = "coral"))
```

## SNV grouping

Reads can also be split by the base they carry at a heterozygous SNV with
`snv = list(position =, ref =, alt =)`. Reads with the `ref` base form group
`"REF"`, reads with the `alt` base form `"ALT"`, and all other reads (those
not covering the position, or carrying another base) are dropped.

```{r read-snv}
meth_snv = read_methylation(
  bam, region,
  snv = list(position = 3000, ref = "A", alt = "G"),
  seed = 1
)
meth_snv
```

```{r plot-snv}
plot_methylation(meth_snv)
```

A dashed vertical line marks the SNV position in the read panel at the top
and in the smooth panel below it, where the REF and ALT curves are overlaid
for direct comparison.

## Binary calls

By default sites are coloured by a continuous probability gradient and the
smooth panel shows the mean probability. Setting `call_threshold` switches to
binary calls: sites at or above the threshold are methylated, the rest
unmethylated, and the smooth panel shows the fraction of methylated calls.
`call_ambiguous = w` labels calls within `w` of the threshold as ambiguous
and leaves them out of that fraction.

```{r plot-binary}
plot_methylation(meth_hp, call_threshold = 0.5, call_ambiguous = 0.1)
```

## Several modification codes

`mod_code` takes several codes at once. Each read bar is then split into one
strip per code (in the order given, top to bottom) and the smooth panel draws
one line per code, distinguished by line type.

```{r plot-two-codes}
meth_mh = read_methylation(bam, region, mod_code = c("m", "h"),
                           group_tag = "HP", seed = 1)
plot_methylation(meth_mh)
```

## Multi-sample comparison

`merge_methylation()` combines named `methylation_data` objects for the same
region and modification code(s); `plot_methylation()` then draws one read
panel per sample above a shared smooth panel. Here two random subsets of the
example BAM stand in for two samples (e.g. tumour and normal).

```{r multi-sample, fig.height = 7}
sample_a = read_methylation(bam, region, group_tag = "HP",
                            max_reads = 40, seed = 1)
sample_b = read_methylation(bam, region, group_tag = "HP",
                            max_reads = 40, seed = 2)
merged = merge_methylation(sample_A = sample_a, sample_B = sample_b)
merged
plot_methylation(merged)
```

## VCF variant overlay

`read_variants()` reads the VCF records in a region (it needs the
`VariantAnnotation` and `SummarizedExperiment` packages), and
`plot_methylation(variants = )` overlays them on the read panel:

- **SNV**: a small black asterisk on each read whose base equals the ALT
  allele;
- **DEL, DUP, INV** (symbolic SVs): a styled segment on every read
  overlapping the SV span (DEL a dark red line with end ticks, DUP two teal
  parallel lines, INV a purple dashed line), with chevrons where the span is
  cut at the region edge;
- **BND**: a label `⋈ mate_chrom:mate_pos` at the bottom of the read panel,
  plus a coloured border on the SA marker of reads whose supplementary
  alignment matches the breakend mate within `bnd_match_tol` (only with
  `show_supplementary = TRUE`, the default).

Short insertions, deletions and MNVs, and symbolic types other than
DEL/DUP/INV, are not drawn.

```{r vcf-overlay, eval = has_variants}
vars = read_variants(vcf, region)
vars
plot_methylation(meth_hp, variants = vars)
```

## Gene annotation track

`read_annotations()` loads gene models from a `TxDb` object or a GTF/GFF file
(via `GenomicFeatures`, `txdbmaker` and `rtracklayer`), and
`plot_methylation(annotations = )` adds them as a track at the top of the
figure. A parsed GTF is cached for the rest of the R session;
`clear_annotation_cache()` frees it. The example data has no gene models, so
this chunk is not run.

```{r gene-track, eval = FALSE}
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene)

md = read_methylation("sample.bam", "chr21:10000000-10050000")
annot = read_annotations(
  txdb   = TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene,
  region = "chr21:10000000-10050000"
)
plot_methylation(md, annotations = annot)
```

## Insertion loci

`read_methylation()` keeps modification calls on inserted bases (CIGAR `I`)
in `$insertion_sites`, also available through `insertion_sites()`.
`list_insertion_loci()` clusters the insertions of all reads into loci
(by position first, then by length) and reports, per locus, the reads that
carry it and the non-carriers: reads that span the locus on both sides
without an insertion there. For real ONT/PacBio data, `min_length = 50`
ignores small sequencing-error insertions; the default `min_length = 1`
keeps everything.

```{r insertion-loci}
head(insertion_sites(meth_hp))

loci = list_insertion_loci(meth_hp, min_length = 50)
loci[, c("locus_id", "anchor_pos", "n_carriers", "n_noncarriers",
         "median_length", "mean_ins_mod_prob")]
```

`plot_insertion_locus()` draws one locus in stitched coordinates: the left
reference flank, the inserted bases (at the locus' median length) and the
right reference flank side by side, with the reads in the top panel
(non-carriers below the carriers) and smoothed modification probabilities
below. The x axis shows reference coordinates in the flanks and the
inserted-base offset in the middle.

```{r plot-insertion}
plot_insertion_locus(meth_hp, loci[1, ], flank = 300)
```

## Customising and composing

`plot_methylation()` exposes the colour gradient, line width, smoothing
span, panel heights and sort order. `panel_heights` gives the relative
heights from top to bottom (read panel, smooth panel, plus the gene track
and delta panel when shown):

```{r custom}
plot_methylation(
  meth_hp,
  colour_low    = "white",
  colour_high   = "darkgreen",
  smooth_span   = 0.4,
  panel_heights = c(2, 2)
)
```

Reads are packed into lanes per group. Within a group they are ordered by
`sort_by`; the default is `"start"` for ungrouped data and
`c("start", "group", "mean_mod_prob")` for grouped data. Any column of
`$reads` can be used, plus `mean_mod_prob` (the per-read mean
probability):

```{r custom-sort}
plot_methylation(meth_hp, sort_by = "mean_mod_prob")
```

The result is a `patchwork` object, so ggplot2 theme calls apply to every
panel with `&`:

```{r compose}
library(ggplot2)
p = plot_methylation(meth)
p & theme(text = element_text(size = 14))
```

Save it with `ggplot2::ggsave()`, giving an explicit size:

```{r ggsave, eval = FALSE}
ggsave("my_methylation_plot.pdf", p, width = 10, height = 6)
```

## Exporting data

`write_methylation()` writes `$reads` and `$sites` to TSV, or the sites to
BED (0-based, score `round(mod_prob * 1000)`, name `<read_name>:<mod_code>`),
optionally gzip-compressed.

```{r write}
prefix = file.path(tempdir(), "synthetic_chr1")
write_methylation(meth_hp, prefix, format = "bed")
list.files(dirname(prefix), pattern = "synthetic_chr1")
readLines(paste0(prefix, "_sites.bed"), n = 3)
```
